propositions.statement:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary z0∈Z; temporarily assume L1: z0∈Ω.
Choose a0∈ℝ satisfying u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)=a0 Uext(z0), whose existence was established in F003.

argument.text: Fix z0∈Z and assume L1: z0∈Ω. The set Ω is open, since positivity is an open condition on the continuous time projection. H001 and the definition of Uext give C∞ regularity on Ω: locally this is exactly the original jointly smooth map, and no value at nonpositive times is used. E004 gives differentiability of Uext there and C∞ regularity of its derivative map. For a constant direction, its constant vector field has zero derivative and all higher derivatives zero; E005 therefore makes evaluation of that derivative map in the direction C∞. Induction repeats E004 and E005 for every finite ordered constant-direction derivative. In particular Uext,u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj have the required derivatives at every positive-time point. For the affine time curve r↦(x,r), the derivative is τ; for the affine spatial curve h↦(x+h ε_j,r), it is σ(j). Their linear remainders are identically zero. E013 applied to Uext, and then to its derivative fields, identifies the directional fields with the ordinary partial derivatives in H001. The curves stay in Ω near each point under consideration. These assertions hold at every point of Ω and for every spatial index.

produces.statement: Uext and every finite ordered constant-direction derivative are C∞ on Ω and differentiable at each point of Ω; u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj there agree with the corresponding ordinary partial derivatives of u.

argument.text: At z0, apply E008 with both factors Uext and direction τ. Real inner-product symmetry and ⟪v,v⟫=‖v‖² give D_τ(⟪Uext,Uext⟫)(z0)=2⟪Uext(z0),u_t(z0)⟫. H002 says ⟪Uext,Uext⟫=1 on the open set Ω. Hence the scalar field agrees with the constant 1 on a neighborhood of z0; E010 identifies its Fréchet derivative with the zero derivative of that constant. Dividing by 2 yields tangency ⟪Uext(z0),u_t(z0)⟫=0.

The acceleration clause of H002 at the positive-time point z0, using the partial-derivative identifications F001 and Δ_xu=Σ_j u_jj, gives a real scalar witness for u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)=a Uext(z0). Record existence before selecting that witness.

produces.statement: There exists a real scalar a with u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)=a Uext(z0).

argument.text: Choose the witness a0 from F003. Taking its inner product with u_t(z0), bilinearity and symmetry give ⟪u_t(z0),u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)⟫=a0⟪u_t(z0),Uext(z0)⟫=0 by F002. This conclusion does not depend on the private choice of a0, so existential elimination removes that witness. No scalar field has been selected and no derivative of a scalar witness has been taken.

Combine F002 and F004, discharge L1 into the condition z0∈Ω, and universally quantify z0. Since Ω is precisely the set of all spatial points and positive times, and F001 identifies every derivative with the original partial derivative, these are both identities of the exported conclusion for every x and t>0, with no scalar regularity assumption.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary t0∈ℝ and assume L1: t0>0.
Choose the compact C0 furnished by F004, for the slab [t0/2,3t0/2].

argument.text: The set Ω is open: it is the inverse image of (0,∞) under the continuous time projection. H001 implies Uext is C∞ on Ω, since it agrees there locally with the original smooth map. E004 supplies differentiability and a smooth derivative map. Evaluate it at any constant direction with E005; constant fields are smooth because their derivatives and all higher derivatives vanish. This makes the directional derivative smooth. Induction repeats these two operations: every finite ordered constant-direction derivative of Uext is C∞ on Ω and differentiable there. At interior points differentiability on the open set is ordinary differentiability. In particular all fields u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj,u_tj are smooth. This argument makes no assertion outside Ω.

produces.statement: Uext and every finite ordered constant-direction derivative are C∞ on Ω, and differentiable at every point of Ω. In particular u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj,u_tj are C∞ there.

argument.text: Apply E009 to each pair defining T,A_j,B_j,H_j and to the repeated factors u_t,u_t and u_j,u_j. The identity ⟪v,v⟫=‖v‖² identifies the latter scalar fields with the squared norms. E014 sums the finite family consisting of the time square and the n spatial squares, giving smoothness of e with precisely its stated normalization. Apply E004 to this scalar e and E005 to its derivative map and the constant τ to obtain smoothness of e_t=Ddir(τ,e). Thus every scalar field in the exported conclusion is jointly smooth on Ω, as are the vector derivative fields already established.

produces.statement: The scalar fields T,A_j,B_j,H_j,e,e_t are C∞ on Ω and consequently continuous and differentiable at each point of Ω.

argument.text: For every z∈Ω and fixed constant directions v,w∈Z, apply E007 to the derivative map of Uext and the constant field with value v. The derivative of that constant field is zero, so evaluating the resulting equality in w gives D_w(D_v Uext)(z)=(fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Uext) z)(w)(v). The derivative map is differentiable by F001 and E004, since it is smooth on the open Ω. Smoothness also gives C² regularity at z. E006 therefore interchanges w and v in the second Fréchet derivative, yielding D_wD_v Uext(z)=D_vD_w Uext(z). Taking v=σ(j) and w=τ for each j proves Ddir(τ,u_j(j))=u_tj(j) throughout Ω. This is a proved mixed-direction identity, rather than a property of the notation.

produces.statement: For every z∈Ω and j∈Fin n, Ddir(τ,u_j(j))(z)=u_tj(j)(z). More generally finite second derivatives in two constant directions commute on Ω.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0 and assume L1: t0>0. Then 0<t0/2<3t0/2, and H003 applied to these endpoints gives existence of a compact spatial set on whose complement u=q throughout [t0/2,3t0/2]. Record this existence before choosing a set.

produces.statement: There exists a compact subset C of X such that u(x,r)=q whenever x∉C and r∈[t0/2,3t0/2].

argument.text: Choose C0 from F004 and define O0=(X∖C0)×(t0/2,3t0/2). A compact subset of Euclidean space is closed and Borel measurable; hence O0 is open. The interval in this product is contained in (0,∞), so O0⊂Ω, and Uext=q on O0 by the choice of C0. These are the only properties of C0 used: no boundary smoothness or nonempty interior is required.

produces.statement: C0 is compact, closed and Lebesgue measurable; O0 is open, contained in Ω, and Uext=q on O0.

argument.text: At every point of O0, E010 compares Uext with the constant q on an open neighborhood, giving zero derivative. This conclusion holds throughout the same open set, so apply E010 again to each first derivative field and the zero field. Inductively, if an ordered positive-order derivative field is identically zero on O0, E010 makes its derivative zero there as well. This proves vanishing of every positive-order derivative of Uext on O0. The same locality argument compares e with zero on O0: e vanishes there because its vector factors vanish, so e_t vanishes there too. Each of T,A_j,B_j,H_j vanishes by its defining inner product. Thus a single C0 supports all these fields for every time in the open slab.

produces.statement: All positive-order constant-direction derivative fields of Uext and the scalar fields e,e_t,T,A_j,B_j,H_j vanish on O0, equivalently outside C0 at every time in (t0/2,3t0/2).

argument.text: For each fixed positive time, compose each of the smooth spacetime fields with the affine spatial inclusion x↦(x,r). E019 applies with source set all of X and target set Ω: the inclusion has constant derivative and higher derivatives zero, and maps into Ω because r>0. Thus all spatial sections are smooth, in particular continuous. Likewise restriction along r↦(x,r) and E013 identify their time partials with the directional derivatives; E013 on the affine spatial coordinate curves identifies their spatial partials. These affine curves have their indicated constant derivatives with zero remainder. This proves agreement with the original ordinary derivatives in the exported conclusion, including ∂_t e=e_t and, using F003, ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t. For times in the chosen open slab, F006 shows that each positive-order derivative section and each listed scalar section has topological support contained in the closed compact C0. The section of Uext itself is smooth; its value outside C0 is q, and no compact-support claim about Uext is made.

produces.statement: Every listed derivative field, listed scalar field, and finite positive-order derivative has continuous spatial sections, supported in C0 at times r∈(t0/2,3t0/2). Directional and ordinary partial derivatives agree on Ω; in particular ∂_t e=e_t and ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t there.

argument.text: For each real scalar section e(·,r), e_t(·,r), T(·,r), A_j(·,r), B_j(·,r), H_j(·,r) at a time r in the open slab, F007 gives continuity on X and hence on C0. E003 makes its restriction to compact C0 integrable. E012 then makes its C0 indicator integrable on X, and that indicator equals the original section pointwise by F006. This proves integrability of all the scalar products, including the undifferentiated H_j. The same argument applied to the norm of any vector derivative section proves integrability of that norm: the norm is continuous and vanishes off C0. The vector section itself is continuous into a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence strongly measurable; integrability of its norm is precisely the remaining condition for Bochner integrability. This also covers any finite-order derivative field, with its finite-dimensional derivative-tensor codomain. Thus every section meant by the exported conclusion is integrable. The reasoning still applies to an empty C0, when all sections vanish.

produces.statement: At every r∈(t0/2,3t0/2), all listed scalar and vector sections, and all finite positive-order derivative sections of u, are Lebesgue integrable.

argument.text: The chosen C0 witnesses the existential conclusion at this t0 by F005–F008. Existentially quantify the set, discharge L1 into t0>0, and universally quantify t0. F001–F003 and F007 establish the asserted joint smoothness and mixed ordinary partial identity at every positive time, independently of the chosen compact set. This proves every clause of the exported conclusion under exactly H001 and H003.

argument.text: Fix t0∈ℝ and assume L1: t0>0. Use H001 and the conditional statement N002 for the current u. It supplies smoothness on Ω, the identity ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t, integrability of all the listed scalar sections at t0, and existence of a compact spatial set supporting them throughout (t0/2,3t0/2). The fields u_t,u_j,e,e_t,T,A_j are smooth on Ω; ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t there. The spatial density and the scalar product sections at t0 are integrable.

argument.text: Choose C0 from F001. Define eta0=t0/4, I0=(t0−eta0,t0+eta0), K0=C0×[t0−eta0,t0+eta0], Fdens(r)(x)=e(x,r), and Gdens(r)(x)=2T(x,r)+2Σ_j A_j(j)(x,r). Since t0>0, eta0>0 and [t0−eta0,t0+eta0]⊂(t0/2,3t0/2). Thus I0 is a neighborhood of t0 made entirely of positive times; K0 is a compact subset of Ω, by compactness of C0 and of the closed bounded real interval. C0 is closed and Borel measurable in X.

produces.statement: eta0>0, I0 is an open neighborhood of t0, K0 is compact and contained in Ω, C0 is compact and measurable, and the closed time interval defining K0 lies inside (t0/2,3t0/2).

argument.text: For every x∈X and r>0, the open-domain smoothness in F002 and E004 give ordinary Fréchet derivatives of u_t,u_j and e at (x,r). The scalar square of each differentiable vector field is also differentiable: expand the vector increment into its linear derivative term plus a remainder of order o of the increment norm; bilinearity of the inner product gives the linear term twice the inner product of the value with that derivative, and all remaining terms are o of the increment norm. Thus the square fields have actual Fréchet derivatives, as required for the chain rule below. E008 with two factors u_t and direction τ gives the derivative of its squared norm as 2T. With two factors u_j(j), it gives 2⟪u_j(j),Ddir(τ,u_j(j))⟫, which is 2A_j by N002's mixed derivative identity. E013 along the affine time curve s↦(x,s), whose derivative is τ with zero affine remainder, converts these directional derivatives to ordinary time derivatives. E015, applied to the finite family with one time term and the n spatial terms, gives HasDerivAt (s↦Fdens(s)(x)) (Gdens(r)(x)) r. Apply E013 also to e itself: its ordinary time derivative is e_t. Uniqueness of ordinary derivatives therefore identifies Gdens(r)(x)=e_t(x,r). In particular the spacetime field (x,r)↦Gdens(r)(x) is jointly continuous on Ω by F002.

produces.statement: At every x∈X and r>0, HasDerivAt (s↦Fdens(s)(x)) (Gdens(r)(x)) r, and Gdens(r)(x)=e_t(x,r). The spacetime Gdens field is continuous on Ω.

argument.text: Use E011 on the compact subset K0 of the real normed space Z and the scalar continuous field (x,r)↦Gdens(r)(x). F003 gives compactness and containment in Ω, and F004 gives continuity there. It yields existence of a finite real bound on |Gdens| throughout K0. This is existence only; select the bound in the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exists b∈ℝ such that |Gdens(r)(x)|≤b for all (x,r)∈K0.

argument.text: Choose b0 from F005 and set B0=max(b0,0), beta0=B0·1_{C0}, where the indicator has value B0 on C0 and zero outside. The constant function B0 is continuous on compact C0, so E003 makes it integrable on C0. Since C0 is measurable by F003, E012 gives integrability on X of its zero extension, which is beta0. Enlarging b0 to B0 preserves its bound even if C0 is empty.

produces.statement: B0≥0, beta0 is integrable on X, and |Gdens(r)(x)|≤B0 for every (x,r)∈K0.

argument.text: For every x∈X and r∈I0, if x∈C0 then (x,r)∈K0 and F006 gives |Gdens(r)(x)|≤B0=beta0(x). If x∉C0 then every factor T,A_j vanishes by the chosen common support in F001, so Gdens(r)(x)=0=beta0(x). Thus the bound holds pointwise for all x and all r∈I0, with a single spatial exceptional set equal to the empty set. For every such r, N002 makes Fdens(r) integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. In particular Fdens(t0) is integrable. F004 identifies Gdens(t0) with e_t(·,t0), whose integrability and hence a.e. strong measurability follow from N002. To make every summand explicit, 2T(·,t0), each 2A_j(·,t0), and their finite sums are continuous scalar sections supported in C0. E003 on C0 and E012 on its zero extension prove all their integrabilities. These applications use no bound uniform over the entire positive-time axis.

produces.statement: For every x and every r∈I0, |Gdens(r)(x)|≤beta0(x). Fdens(r) is a.e. strongly measurable for every r∈I0, Fdens(t0) is integrable, Gdens(t0) is a.e. strongly measurable and integrable, and each displayed derivative summand at t0 is integrable.

argument.text: Apply E001 with spatial dimension n, F=Fdens, G=Gdens, time t0, neighborhood I0, and bound beta0. F003 gives the neighborhood premise. F007 gives measurability of the density for every time in that neighborhood, its integrability at t0, and a.e. strong measurability of Gdens(t0). F007 and F006 give respectively the common pointwise bound and integrability of the bound. F004 gives the ordinary time derivative at every x and r∈I0, hence with a single full-measure spatial set. Thus all seven premises are satisfied. E001 returns integrability of Gdens(t0) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫_X Fdens(r)(x)dx) (∫_X Gdens(t0)(x)dx) t0. By the definitions of Fdens and E, this is the derivative of E itself.

produces.statement: E has ordinary derivative ∫_X Gdens(t0)(x)dx at t0, and Gdens(t0) is integrable.

argument.text: Insert the explicit definition of Gdens into F008. F002 gives integrability of the actual density at t0, and F007 gives integrability of each derivative summand. Eliminate the compact-set and bound witnesses, which do not occur in this assertion. Discharge L1 into the condition t0>0 and universally quantify t0. All derivative arguments took place in a positive open neighborhood, so changing the total representative at nonpositive times has no effect on this derivative. This is precisely the exported conclusion, for the actual finite integral with coefficient 1 in each square and coefficient 2 in its derivative.

The inclusion is smooth (constant first derivative, zero higher derivatives) and maps all of X into Ω because t0>0. Hence f0 and g0 are globally smooth spatial maps, and thus differentiable at every point of X.

argument.text: For every x∈X compare the same real-parameter curve in two ways. E013 applied to f0 and the affine spatial curve h↦x+h v0 gives derivative Ddir(v0,f0)(x) at h=0. Applied to u_t and the spacetime curve h↦(x+h v0,t0), it gives u_tj(j0)(x,t0). The composed functions are identical by definition of f0; uniqueness of ordinary derivatives gives Ddir(v0,f0)(x)=u_tj(j0)(x,t0). Both curves have the indicated derivatives v0 and σ(j0) with zero affine remainder. Repeat with g0 and u_j(j0); the directional derivative is u_jj(j0)(x,t0). All requisite spacetime derivatives exist by N002's smoothness on the open Ω, and all spatial derivatives by F001. Thus the directional derivatives used for integration by parts are precisely the intended partial derivatives, without requiring a general unrecorded change of domain.

argument.text: N002 at t0 gives integrability of A_j(j0)(·,t0), B_j(j0)(·,t0), and H_j(j0)(·,t0). F001 gives differentiability of f0 on the entire spatial domain, hence on the topological support of g0, and similarly for g0 on the support of f0. E002 with dimensions n,m, maps f0,g0 and direction v0 is therefore applicable and returns ∫_X B_j(j0)(x,t0)dx=−∫_X A_j(j0)(x,t0)dx.

argument.text: Work with the original data H001,H002,H003: n,m≥1, jointly smooth u, the fixed unit q, the unit constraint and pointwise normal acceleration, and common compact support of the perturbation from q on every closed positive-time slab. This is exactly the selected interpretation of spatial compact support. Fix arbitrary t0 and assume L1: t0>0. N002 and N003 apply to these data: e(·,t0) and T(·,t0), every A_j(·,t0) and B_j(·,t0) are integrable, and E has ordinary derivative ∫_X(2T+2Σ_j A_j)(x,t0)dx at t0. argument.text: All operations here involve finitely many integrable real sections from F001. Finite sums and constant multiples remain integrable: their absolute values are bounded by the finite sum of the absolute values of the summands, multiplied by the absolute constants, and the corresponding measurability and finite-integral conditions follow. E018 splits the integral into the 2T part and the 2Σ_j A_j part. E017 with c=2 extracts each factor 2, and E016 moves the finite spatial sum through its integral. Hence the derivative value in F001 is 2∫_X T(x,t0)dx+2Σ_j∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx. There is no limiting infinite sum.

produces.statement: HasDerivAt E (2∫_X T(x,t0)dx+2Σ_{j∈Fin n}∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx) t0.

argument.text: N004 at t0 gives ∫_X A_j(j)(x,t0)dx=−∫_X B_j(j)(x,t0)dx for each j∈Fin n, with both integrands integrable. Substitute these finitely many equalities into F002 and distribute the finite minus sign. The derivative value is therefore 2∫T−2Σ_j∫B_j.
